description: FICTIONAL EXERCISE. Overnight rain has flooded low streets in Riverbend. Power is out and tap water is unavailable. The house is dry now, but water is visible at the end of the street. The household needs a safe plan for the next 24 hours, especially drinking water. No one is currently injured or reporting acute symptoms.

location.home: Two-story house, bedrooms upstairs, no basement, ground-floor accessible bedroom and bathroom
location.hazard_context: Low-lying neighborhood near a fictional river; no verified safe route is supplied
location.meeting_point: Upstairs landing only if accessible and safe; outdoor reunion location must be confirmed locally

household.name: Maya
household.health: Asthma; prescribed rescue inhaler and spacer available; follow existing clinician action plan

household.name: Ruth
household.health: Routine daily medication available for 7 days; no powered medical device
household.mobility: Uses a walker; stairs require assistance and may not be safe

resources.other_water: No safe tap supply; rain barrel water is untreated and potentially contaminated
resources.food: Two days of shelf-stable, ready-to-eat food for four; manual can opener
resources.lighting: Two battery torches; spare batteries; no need for candles
resources.communications: Battery AM/FM weather radio, two phones at 65% and 40%, one fully charged 10000 mAh power bank; mobile service intermittent
resources.navigation: Paper street map and compass; neither proves a route is flood-free
resources.medical: Basic first-aid kit, prescribed rescue inhaler with spacer, 7-day routine medication supply, printed medication list
resources.transport: One car with half a tank, parked on dry driveway; route safety unknown
resources.sanitation: Soap, hand sanitizer, rubbish bags, gloves; toilets may become unusable if sewers back up
resources.shelter: Blankets, warm clothes, waterproof jackets, walker; no generator or indoor fuel-burning equipment

skills.expertise: Basic first-aid course last year; can monitor the radio and pack medication
Camping experience, paper-map reading, household inventory and phone charging
Knows household medication routines; can help maintain a written check-in list
Can choose comfort items and tell an adult if breathing changes; no hazardous tasks

priorities: Obtain verified safe drinking water without hazardous travel
Plan accessible evacuation before conditions worsen
Keep family calm and monitor health
unknowns: Actual shelter accessibility and opening status
